text:
kevin: Heads-up — sketching a telemetry surface for Private / air-gapped enclaves. TL;DR: minimal local envelope + deferred enrichment when a gateway or manual push is available. Wanted quick feedback.

maya: Clarifying Q — 'enclave' = VPC-only private control plane, or fully air-gapped on-prem installs too?

kevin: Both. Primary target is fully air-gapped on-prem where outbound egress is disabled. Secondary is VPC-private with restricted egress. Constraints: no live billing lookup, no external enrichment, and potentially months of offline buffering.

sam: Sounds right. That implies two modes: local telemetry with retention + a manifest/push model for sending data back to Redwood. How do we keep cost attribution without sending tenant IDs?

jess: Proposal: locally store a minimal envelope per span/trace. Keep fields that are necessary for later attribution/enrichment but exclude raw customer identifiers and PII. Example minimal keys:

```
{
  "trace_id": "...",
  "span_id": "...",
  "service": "svc-name",
  "op": "generate",    // e.g., generate, embed, rerank
  "ts": 1680000000,
  "seq_len_hint": 512,  // token-length hint
  "model_hint": "gptx-13b-quant", // free text
  "sampling_decision": "keep|drop",
  "billing_key_hmac": "sha256:hmac", // HMAC of tenant billing key
  "tokens_hint": 123, // approximate tokens
  "error_flag": false
}
```

kevin: Key is to keep only deterministic, non-PII hints. Use an HMAC of the tenant billing key (customer-managed key) so Redwood can map to tenant on ingest without raw IDs. HSM/KMS handshake required.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: created telemetry buffer at /var/lib/redwood/tm_buffer size=50GB retention=7d (default)

maya: Edge cases: if network is down for months, the manifest will be huge. We need chunked manifests, resumable uploads, and server-side dedupe + ordering guarantees. Also expose backpressure so local services can throttle.

sam: Agree. Implementation notes: chunk manifests and include checkpoints with monotonic counters. When manifest arrives, validate signature (customer KMS/HSM) and verify HMACs. Only after verification do we join with billing records.

jess: Sampling: deterministic sampling is crucial for later trace joinability. Use trace_id modulo N deterministic sampler (configurable per enclave). Store sampling_config_version in envelope.

kevin: Decision sketch (please call out objections):
1) Local storage = minimal envelope only (no request/response bodies, no raw tenant ids)
2) Billing attribution via tenant-billing-key HMAC; mapping happens on Redwood ingest after signature verification
3) Deterministic sampling by trace_id (configurable rate)
4) Deferred enrichment — Redwood runs enrichment (lookup full tenant, model mappings, user mappings) post-ingest from manifest chunks
5) Manifest upload is chunked/resumable, signed by customer key (HSM/KMS), and supports checkpointing for resume/dedupe
6) Add a small local aggregator that emits encrypted model-usage counters (no content, only aggregate counts) for near-term cost visibility

maya: +1 for 1–6. A couple follow-ups: what about latency SLOs for on-prem monitoring (alerts)? Customers still need near-realtime health alerts even offline. We should support local alerting rules and an option to push notifications to a configured pager endpoint (customer-owned).

sam: Security note: HMAC approach is fine but keys must never leave HSM. We should define a handshake: enroll enclave public key in Redwood, Redwood provides a challenge, enclave signs nonce with KMS, Redwood binds billing-hash to account. Drafting handshake doc (security).

jess: Implementation owners / next steps:
- kevin: draft the enclave-telemetry-surface RFC (include envelope schema + sampling contract + upload protocol)
- eng-runtime: implement buffer + chunked manifest uploader with resumable protocol (suggest S3 multipart style + server-side checkpointing)
- security: KMS/HSM handshake and verification flow (must include replay protection)
- eng-platform: design server-side ingest path for chunked manifests + HMAC mapping + enrichment pipeline

kevin: One more operational detail — when doing deferred enrichment, we should keep an audit trail that shows which manifest chunk produced which enriched spans for debugging. Keep a manifest_id in all envelopes.

maya: +thumbsup: also add a knob to drop all telemetry if disk usage exceeds threshold (fail-open vs fail-closed discussion). My preference: fail-open on app (i.e., stop buffering, add local stats to indicate drop), but surface this to ops.

kevin: Good point. For now default = graceful drop (emit telemetry-drop events locally). We'll surface counts in the aggregate upload.

sam: Also consider retention-policy: default 7d, configurable up to 90d with local storage limits enforced. Document recommended disk-per-requests guidance in RFC.

jess: I'll add those to the action list.

kevin: Thanks — i'll do a first RFC draft by EOD Thursday. If you have examples of minimal envelopes from other air-gapped products, paste them here. :pray:
